For \(n\ge 2\), \(a_1=2^n\). Since \(2^k \pmod{100}\) has period \(20\) for \(k\ge 2\), we check \(a_2 \pmod{100}\). We have
\[
a_1 \equiv 4,8,16,12 \pmod{20}
\]
depending on \(n\), so
\[
a_2 \equiv 2^4,2^8,2^{16},2^{12} \equiv 16,56,36,96 \pmod{100}.
\]
All are \(\equiv 16 \pmod{20}\). Hence
\[
a_i \equiv 2^{16}\equiv 36 \pmod{100}
\]
for all \(i\ge 3\). Thus for \(n\ge 2\),
\[
a_{1000}\equiv 36 \pmod{100}.
\]
The condition becomes
\[
a_1=2^n \equiv 36 \pmod{100}.
\]
This happens when \(n\equiv 16\pmod{20}\). For \(1\le n\le 1000\), these are
\[
16,36,\ldots,996,
\]
which are \(50\) integers.

For \(n=1\), \(a_1=2\), while \(a_{1000}\equiv 36\pmod{100}\), so it does not work.

\[
\boxed{50}
\]
